blocks.text:
This active itinerary alternates between cities and the outdoors. You’ll go up to Christ the Redeemer and Sugarloaf Mountain, ride a jeep through Tijuca Forest, spend a day exploring the bays of Ilha Grande and see Iguazu Falls. You can also get closer to the falls by boat on the optional Macuco Safari. In the Pantanal, the focus shifts to wildlife, open plains and early-morning safaris. In Bonito, you’ll find clear water, limestone caves, rafting and ziplining. The trip ends among the white dunes and lagoons of Lençóis Maranhenses.

The landscape changes almost every time you move on. The lush, humid Tijuca Forest starts right inside the city. Car-free Ilha Grande is a place of trails, boats and small bays. At Iguazu, it’s the sheer volume of falling water that stands out. The Pantanal gives you a rare chance to watch wildlife in open country, while the clarity of Bonito’s rivers shapes much of your time there. Lençóis is different again, with white sand, wind and blue lagoons between the dunes.
